alberta_selection.reason_selected: Red Deer and Central Alberta searches produced important cultural-safety concerns and current support services, but no equally strong incident-to-investigation-to-response chain. The provincewide panel was selected because it provides 22 recommendations, a formal implementation plan, funding mechanisms, an oversight/complaint function and later follow-up.

owner_view.what_happened: Alberta convened an Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel that produced 22 recommendations for culturally safe, Indigenous-led and accountable primary health care. Government then published an implementation plan and created or funded several mechanisms, including an Indigenous Health Division, navigator grants, an innovation fund and an Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate.
why_this_matters: It is Alberta's strongest defensible public chain from Indigenous-led advice to government commitments and operational mechanisms.
It shows why a program, funding stream and complaints office should remain separate evidence stages.
The Red Deer search still yielded useful local context, while avoiding a forced weak local case.
review_first: Multiple implementation mechanisms are verifiable, but no current comprehensive public status ledger for all 22 recommendations was located.
The Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate is operational with defined powers and limits; it is not a court, professional regulator or substitute for every complaint route.
Navigator and innovation funding are implementation evidence, not evidence of provincewide access or outcomes.
review_next: Map the 22 recommendations to The Way Forward milestones.
Assess which funded recipients serve Central Alberta.
Track the promised anti-racism strategy following 2024 engagement.
Keep Treaty 6, 7 and 8 references as governance/territorial context unless a source establishes a specific legal consequence.
reference: Red Deer hospital support services are operational context but were not linked to a specific triggering accountability action in public sources.
what_we_know: Government published a separate Indigenous implementation plan.
Current pages document funding and oversight mechanisms.
The patient-safety advocate has a Health Charter review and advisory role with explicit limits.
what_remains_uncertain: Current status of each of the 22 recommendations.
Geographic distribution and sustained operation of all funded initiatives.
Outcome evidence for navigator, innovation and complaint mechanisms.
Whether the anti-racism engagement produced a final strategy after the last public update.
next_questions: Is there a current internal or public 22-recommendation implementation ledger?
Which panel-funded initiatives provide verified service in Red Deer or Central Zone?
owner_view.recommended_next_move: Build a 22-recommendation public-evidence ledger using The Way Forward, then verify Central Alberta recipients and services as a separate bounded pass.
owner_view.one_thing_to_remember: Alberta publicly demonstrates implementation machinery, but not yet one complete public account of the status and outcomes of all 22 recommendations.

implementation_evidence.summary: The Way Forward is a formal response plan tied to the panel recommendations.
Navigator and innovation funding mechanisms are publicly documented.
The Indigenous Health Division and Indigenous Patient Safety Investigator and Advocate are documented structures.
The advocate provides a current complaint-support and system-advice mechanism with specified powers and limits.
Current government pages list completed and underway actions, but not a complete current 22-row status ledger.

follow_up_and_recurrence.title: Anti-racism engagement
follow_up_and_recurrence.summary: Later engagement revisits racism in Indigenous health care; this is a follow-up signal, not proof that earlier mechanisms were ineffective.

follow_up_and_recurrence.title: Red Deer local services
follow_up_and_recurrence.summary: Indigenous hospital support is operational at RDRHC, but no source-backed edge to a panel commitment was located in this pass.

edges.neutral_summary: The implementation plan is a formal government response.
Government reports the division as an implementation structure.
Navigator grants operationalize part of access and navigation recommendations.
The fund supports implementation projects; program-level funding is not service-level attribution.
The advocate is a current oversight and complaint-support mechanism.
The advocate may undertake delegated Health Charter reviews within defined limits.
Later engagement documents continuing policy attention without proving earlier reform failure.
The service establishes local operational context but is not attributed to the panel without evidence.

findings.title: Panel recommendations connect to real mechanisms
findings.summary: A formal plan, funding programs, a ministry division and an advocate are source-backed.
findings.why_it_matters: The chain reaches beyond announcement into administration and operation.
findings.uncertainty: It does not establish all recommendations complete or effective.

findings.title: Comprehensive recommendation reporting remains unclear
findings.summary: No current public 22-row status ledger was located.
findings.why_it_matters: It prevents overgeneralizing from selected programs.
findings.recommended_action: Ask Alberta Health for a current crosswalk.

findings.title: The discovery process correctly rejected a forced Red Deer case
findings.summary: Local official sources showed concern and services but not a deep accountability chain.
findings.why_it_matters: Evidence quality took priority over geographic preference.
findings.uncertainty: Local links may emerge in a future recipient/service pass.
findings.recommended_action: Retain Red Deer candidates as context, not as the dossier anchor.

findings.title: Advocate powers and limits are explicit
findings.summary: The current office supports complaints and delegated Charter reviews but cannot exercise court or regulator powers.
findings.why_it_matters: Clear boundaries prevent overstating accountability authority.
findings.recommended_action: Display mandate limits beside the mechanism.

findings.title: Later engagement revisits racism concerns
findings.summary: The 2024 engagement is a later related signal.
findings.why_it_matters: It may guide the next policy follow-up.
findings.uncertainty: It is not proof the panel response failed.
findings.recommended_action: Track publication of the resulting strategy.

knowledge_gap_follow_ups.question: Is there a current comprehensive public status ledger for all 22 Indigenous Primary Health Care Advisory Panel recommendations?
knowledge_gap_follow_ups.answer: Government sources document a dedicated implementation plan and multiple current mechanisms, but no comprehensive current recommendation-by-recommendation status ledger was located.
knowledge_gap_follow_ups.stopping_reason: The central official report, implementation plan and current program pages were inspected. Additional searches repeated the same sources and showed diminishing returns; organization-specific follow-up is the appropriate next step.

owner_assessment.owner_review_reason: The 22 recommendation crosswalk, Central Alberta recipient mapping and anti-racism strategy status remain unresolved.
owner_assessment.recommended_next_action: Create the 22-recommendation ledger and a separate Central Alberta recipient/service map.

limitations: This is a policy and implementation dossier, not an adjudicated incident case. It does not infer legal consequences from Treaty geography, effectiveness from program creation, or a direct causal link between Red Deer services and panel recommendations without evidence.
